static_content.text: "you are not under the law, but under grace."

Being under grace is not like being under the law. Under the Law, a violation would result in death with no exceptions. Under grace, those in Christ are expected to perform work as a slave to righteousness, but you are given help - Christ the vine-keeper fertilizes and massages the soil. You are expected to eventually produce fruit.

Under grace, failing to produce fruit is not a direct equation resulting in death - as the parable implies, death or fire could eventually result but not right away because Christ is interceding. This is why it is called "grace and faith" - The law of faith is the grace. Under Moral and Commandment Law, violations cause sin which causes death.

Therefore the world is dead because of sin which is the infection that kills all of humanity due to a guilty conscience. The Church is never infected with sin due to Christ but members can still potentially die from a lack of effort/fruit. Therefore we work out our salvation with fear and trembling, not because of a fear of sin, but fear of living up to responsibility in the vineyard. There are many instances one can shirk the responsibility of being a slave to righteousness, for example, by ceasing to eat the spiritual meal (communion) which would eventually cause a death...again not because of sin but because weakness due to starvation. Those in Christ never sin once they are born of Him (1 John 5:18). This is why Church members should not fear sin but should fear judgment because "anything is permissible, but not everything is beneficial." Only under grace can that statement be true.
